title: [Flight] Allow dev tooling to provide a scoped evaluator for debug-only eval
body:
## Summary

In dev, the Flight client uses `eval` to rebuild server stack frames. Runtimes that block `eval`, like workerd, fall back to frames that lose the server file, line and column. Some of these runtimes still offer a dev-only scoped evaluator. For example, the Cloudflare Vite plugin gives each runner worker workerd's `UnsafeEval` binding.

This PR lets tooling install one at `globalThis[Symbol.for('react.debug_eval')]`:

```js
globalThis[Symbol.for('react.debug_eval')] = (code) => env.__VITE_UNSAFE_EVAL__.eval(code);
```

If the hook is set, React's dev-only eval sites and `checkEvalAvailabilityOnceDev` use it instead of global `eval`. There's no change in production or when the hook isn't set.

## How did you test this change?

- New test in `ReactFlight-test.js`: with `eval` disabled and the hook set, error stack frames point to the server source. It fails if the hook is ignored.
- New test in `ReactFlightDOMReplyEdge-test.js`: with the hook set, there's no eval warning.
- `yarn test` and `yarn test --prod` pass on the affected Flight suites. `yarn flow` (dom-node, dom-browser, dom-edge-webpack, custom, noop), `yarn linc` and `yarn prettier` are clean.

title: [compiler] Don't treat use-named constants and properties as hooks
body:
Fixes #29900.

Related: #30493 (same validator, reported through eslint-plugin-react-compiler). I did not reproduce #30493 separately, and this PR does not claim to close it.

## Summary

The compiler decided whether a value is a hook from its name alone in three places, so valid code that maps over a `use*`-named constant or property failed to compile:

- A module-level constant (`const useCases = [...]`) got a hook type from its name, so using it as a method receiver or as a value reported "Hooks may not be referenced as normal values".
- A hook-named property of a module-level object (`thisIsSafeBut.useCases.map(...)`) was treated as a known hook, producing the same error.
- A `PotentialHook` value (for example `props.useItems`, or a local named `useItems`) passed the hook kind to every property, so `props.useItems.map(...)` was reported as a dynamic or conditional hook call.

Changes in `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler`:

- `HIRBuilder.ts` / `HIR.ts`: a module-level binding that is never reassigned and is initialized to a literal, array, or object is marked `isNonHookConstant` (a new optional field on the `ModuleLocal` binding).
- `Environment.ts`: `getGlobalDeclaration` gives such bindings no name-based hook type.
- `ValidateHooksUsage.ts`: such bindings are `Local` rather than `Global`. Property and destructure reads from a `PotentialHook` keep the hook kind only when the property name is hook-like, matching the existing `Local` branch.

The Rust port mirrors the same rules in a second commit (`[rust-compiler]`): `compiler/crates/*` and `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler-rust/src/scope.ts`. The scope info carries `isNonHookConstant`, and the Rust hooks validator applies the same logic, so the `React Compiler (Rust)` job passes. The new fixture's expected input is refreshed to the formatted source that the snapshot runners compare.

What stays the same:

- Real hook calls and module-level hook functions and arrow functions are still validated (conditional and dynamic calls, and hooks passed as values).
- A hook used as a method receiver, such as `useFoo.call(null)` inside a condition, still errors.
- No existing `.expect.md` output changed.

Known gap, unchanged and pinned by existing fixtures: a hook-named property of an undeclared global or unknown import used as a value (`Foo.useCases` where `Foo` is not declared) still reports the error, the same as `Foo.useFoo` in `error.propertyload-hook`.

## How did you test this change?

I reproduced the bug first with fixtures that fail before the fix. The issue's playground code produces the two "referenced as normal values" errors. The new fixtures also fail on valid code before the fix: `props.useItems.map` reports "Hooks must be the same function on every render", and a ternary around it reports "Hooks must always be called in a consistent order". Those same fixtures pass after the fix.

New fixtures (under `compiler/packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler/src/__tests__/fixtures/compiler/`): `use-named-module-constant-not-hook`, `use-named-property-not-hook`, `use-named-constant-as-prop-not-hook`, and the guards `error.module-local-hook-as-prop` and `error.module-local-arrow-hook-conditional`.

Commands, all on Linux (Node 20.19.2, yarn 1.22.22):

```
cd compiler && yarn snap                                 # 1841 tests, 1841 passed, 0 failed
yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler lint          # pass
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/babel-plugin-react-compiler  # pass
yarn workspace babel-plugin-react-compiler jest          # 16 suites, 44 tests passed
./scripts/react-compiler/build-compiler.sh && ./scripts/react-compiler/link-compiler.sh \
  && yarn workspace eslint-plugin-react-hooks test       # 4 suites, 5086 tests passed
cd .. && yarn prettier && yarn linc                      # pass
yarn flow dom-node                                       # pass
yarn test ReactHooks  /  yarn test-www ReactHooks        # pass (source and www)

# Rust port (the "React Compiler (Rust)" job, run in CI order)
cargo check && cargo build && cargo fmt --check          # pass
bash compiler/scripts/test-babel-ast.sh                  # pass
bash compiler/scripts/test-rust-port.sh                  # 1840 passed, 0 failed
yarn workspace snap run build && yarn snap --rust        # 1841 passed, 0 failed
```

Not run: the devtools `compiler-integration` test, which needs a full `yarn test --build`. Its inputs use only `React.useState`, so this change does not reach it.

## Unapplied review findings

- [ ] needs-human: `error.propertyload-hook.js` and `error.hook-property-load-local-hook.js` pin that a hook-named property of an undeclared global or unknown import used as a value is an error. Changing that reverses a deliberate behavior, so it needs a decision. Options: keep the current behavior, or relax value references for such properties and update `error.propertyload-hook`.

title: [DOM] Re-enable events while a View Transition is waiting to start
body:
## Summary

Fixes #37997

When a commit starts a View Transition, the mutation phase is deferred until the browser calls the `startViewTransition` update callback, which can be several frames later. The before-mutation phase has already called `prepareForCommit` by then, which disables the event system. `resetAfterCommit` doesn't run until the mutation phase, so events stay disabled for the whole wait.

Keystrokes in a controlled input during that window never reach `onChange`, so the input loses characters. This happens in the issue's repro, where a `useDeferredValue` list wrapped in `<ViewTransition>` refreshes while someone types.

This PR:

- Calls `resetAfterCommit` after before-mutation when a View Transition is starting. That re-enables events and restores the selection.
- Calls `prepareForCommit` again right before the mutation phase runs.

If an event fires during the wait, `finishEventHandler` calls `flushSyncWork`. That cancels the pending transition and commits the held work, so the keystroke interrupts the animation instead of being dropped. This matches how typing behaves without `<ViewTransition>`.

### Notes for reviewers

- Typing during the start window now cancels the View Transition, so that animation is skipped.
- The existing DEV warning ("A flushSync update cancelled a View Transition…") will also fire in this case. Its wording mentions `flushSync`, which may be misleading when a keystroke triggers it.
- The return value of the second `prepareForCommit` call (`activeInstance`, used with `enableCreateEventHandleAPI`) is ignored. It is only used for before-blur handling, which already ran in the first phase.

## How did you test this change?

- Added a regression test in `ReactDOMViewTransition-test.js`, using a mocked `startViewTransition` that holds `update()`. It fails without the change (`onChange` called 0 times) and passes with it.
- Ran the `react-dom` and `react-reconciler` suites, plus `yarn test --prod` (covering only `react-dom` and `react-reconciler`, not the whole repo), `yarn linc`, `yarn prettier` and `yarn flow dom-node`. `ReactDOMFizzShellHydration` ("recovers from a large component stack during SSR") fails with and without this change.
- Ran the issue's repro in Chrome with Playwright against a production build, with delays of 0–60 ms. Input was lost in 5 of 21 trials without the change and 0 of 21 with it.
